learningObjectives.title: The West and the Plains Indians: way of life, beliefs and society
Migration and early settlement: Manifest Destiny, Mormons and the Gold Rush
The American Civil War: causes, course and consequences
Settlement and the changing way of life: railroads, homesteaders and cattle
Conflict and conquest: the Indian Wars and the end of the frontier

questions.q: In which year was the phrase 'Manifest Destiny' first coined?
questions.explain: The journalist John O'Sullivan coined the phrase in 1845 to express the belief that white Americans were destined to settle the whole continent.

questions.q: In which year did the California Gold Rush begin, drawing the 'forty-niners' west?
questions.explain: Although gold was discovered in 1848, the mass migration of prospectors known as 'forty-niners' took place in 1849.

questions.q: Which animal was central to the way of life of the Plains Indians, providing food, clothing and shelter?
options: The horse
The buffalo
The deer
The ox
questions.explain: The buffalo provided the Plains Indians with meat, hides for tepees and clothing, and materials for tools and utensils.

questions.q: In which year did the American Civil War begin?
questions.explain: The war began in 1861 when Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter following the secession of the southern states.

questions.q: In which year was the Emancipation Proclamation issued?
questions.explain: President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on 1 January 1863.

questions.q: How many acres of land did the Homestead Act of 1862 grant to a settler?
questions.explain: Settlers received 160 acres and could gain full ownership after living on and farming the land for five years.

questions.q: In which year did the Battle of the Little Bighorn take place?
questions.explain: In 1876 Custer's 7th Cavalry was wiped out by Sioux and Cheyenne warriors led by Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse.

questions.q: In which year did the massacre at Wounded Knee occur?
questions.explain: The massacre at Wounded Knee took place in 1890 and effectively ended armed Plains Indian resistance.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the Plains Indians' attitude towards land?
options: Land could be bought and sold for profit
Land was sacred and could not be owned by individuals
Land belonged only to tribal chiefs
Land should be fenced off and farmed intensively
questions.explain: The Plains Indians believed the land and nature were sacred and could not be individually owned, which brought them into conflict with settlers.

questions.q: Why was the horse so significant for the Plains Indians' way of life?
options: It allowed them to build permanent stone settlements
It enabled them to hunt buffalo more effectively and travel greater distances
It replaced the buffalo as their main source of food
It ended all warfare between rival tribes
questions.explain: The horse made the Plains Indians highly mobile, allowing them to follow and hunt the buffalo herds and to wage war.

questions.q: Why did the Mormons, led by Brigham Young, migrate to the Great Salt Lake in 1847?
options: To search for gold in the Rocky Mountains
To escape religious persecution and settle away from other Americans
To trade furs with the Plains Indians
To build the transcontinental railroad
questions.explain: Facing hostility and violence in the east, the Mormons sought an isolated area where they could practise their religion freely.

questions.q: What was a key economic difference between the northern and southern states before the Civil War?
options: The North was agricultural while the South was industrial
The North relied on slavery while the South opposed it
The North was more industrial while the South depended on slave-based agriculture
Both regions had identical economies based on cattle ranching
questions.explain: The North's economy was increasingly based on industry, while the South relied on plantation agriculture worked by enslaved people.

questions.q: What was significant about the Emancipation Proclamation of 1863?
options: It immediately freed all enslaved people throughout the United States
It declared enslaved people in the Confederate states to be free, making abolition a war aim
It gave all freed slaves the right to vote
It ended the Civil War
questions.explain: The Proclamation applied to states in rebellion and reframed the war as a fight against slavery, though full abolition came with the 13th Amendment in 1865.

questions.q: How did the transcontinental railroad affect the Plains Indians?
options: It had little impact on their way of life
It helped protect the buffalo herds
It brought settlers and hunters who destroyed the buffalo and took their lands
It allowed the Plains Indians to trade goods across the country
questions.explain: The railroad opened the Plains to settlers and buffalo hunters, undermining the Plains Indians' way of life and territory.

questions.q: Why were cattle towns such as Abilene significant in the development of the West?
options: They were where the Plains Indians were forced to live on reservations
They linked cattle from Texas to the railroads, allowing beef to be sold in eastern cities
They were the sites of major Civil War battles
They were mining settlements built during the Gold Rush
questions.explain: Joseph McCoy established Abilene as a railhead where Texas cattle driven north could be shipped east, boosting the cattle industry.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Dawes Act of 1887?
options: To grant the Plains Indians full independence
To break up tribal reservations and force Native Americans to assimilate into white society
To protect the buffalo from extinction
To give the Plains Indians the right to vote
questions.explain: The Act divided reservations into individual allotments to undermine tribal life and encourage assimilation into American society.

questions.q: A group of migrants crossed the Plains safely in 1852 because tribes had agreed to allow travellers to pass in return for payments and clearly defined territories. Which agreement made this possible?
options: The Homestead Act
The Fort Laramie Treaty of 1851
The Dawes Act
The Emancipation Proclamation
questions.explain: The Fort Laramie Treaty of 1851 defined tribal territories and secured safe passage for migrants crossing the Plains.

questions.q: A homesteader on the Great Plains could find little timber to fence their claim and keep out roaming cattle. Which innovation solved this problem?
options: The steel plough
Barbed wire
The windmill
The six-shooter
questions.explain: Barbed wire, patented by Joseph Glidden in 1874, gave homesteaders a cheap way to fence land where wood was scarce.

questions.q: Despite their victory at the Little Bighorn in 1876, the Sioux and Cheyenne were soon defeated. Which factor best explains why?
options: The Plains Indians ran out of horses
Public outrage in the east led the US army to launch a relentless campaign to crush resistance
The tribes signed a peace treaty giving up their lands voluntarily
A disease epidemic wiped out the warriors
questions.explain: The defeat of Custer shocked the American public, prompting a determined military campaign that forced the tribes onto reservations.

questions.q: In 1890 the US army grew alarmed at a Sioux religious movement that promised the return of the buffalo and the disappearance of white settlers. This tension led directly to which event?
options: The Battle of the Little Bighorn
The massacre at Wounded Knee
The signing of the Fort Laramie Treaty
The California Gold Rush
questions.explain: Fear of the Ghost Dance movement led to the confrontation at Wounded Knee, where around 250 Sioux were killed, ending armed resistance.
